title: 100,000-Hour Journey Adjustment Ledger
status: empty reconciliation ledger ready for evidence
purpose: Apply recovered evidence to a declared counting model without rewriting or erasing the underlying flat 18-hour/day baseline.
rule: Every adjustment must identify the period, amount, operation, evidence status and reason. Unverified remembered corrections remain pending and do not alter the reconciled total.

operations.add: Add qualifying hours omitted by the baseline or a prior reconstruction.
operations.deduct: Remove hours that evidence shows should not count under the selected model.
operations.reclassify: Move hours between categories without necessarily changing the total.
operations.deduplicate: Remove duplicated concurrent time when converting platform-hours to wall-clock presence.
operations.boundary_shift: Move the Son/Father partition while preserving the total continuum.
operations.anchor_shift: Change the first-stream anchor; this requires recomputing the flat-model baseline rather than pretending it is an ordinary local correction.

entry_schema.source_rule: A pending-source entry can be preserved for investigation but contributes zero hours to a verified/reconciled total until its counting status is promoted.

derived_totals.note: Populate from ledger entries once primary or sufficiently strong evidence is recovered.

examples.description: Two platforms carried the same six-hour broadcast. A wall-clock model may count six hours while a platform-hour model may count twelve.
A recovered archive proves a 23-hour day where the flat model allocated only 18, yielding a +5-hour adjustment for a reconstructed model.
Evidence shows an entire assumed 18-hour day was offline, yielding a -18-hour adjustment for that reconstruction.
